A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SimULi, with matching methods and main experiments. All pages, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, were available for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original camera and LiDAR reconstruction and novel-view synthesis results on Waymo and PandaSet, alongside component ablations and rendering benchmarks.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds AlignMiF results, projection comparisons and further component analyses.

M1.justification: The factorized Gaussian representation, anchoring loss, unscented projection, tiling, culling and optimization procedures remain unchanged. Appendix A discusses a possible non-spinning LiDAR extension without establishing a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Waymo Interp., Waymo Dynamic and PandaSet on the same reconstruction and novel-view synthesis tasks. Added illustrations examine existing temporal and LiDAR-noise conditions; non-spinning LiDAR is discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v3 adds AlignMiF to the static Waymo Interp. comparison in Table 1. New Table 8 compares SimULi's projection against linearization and Monte Carlo sampling. Existing dynamic benchmark comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Added analyses introduce rolling-shutter on/off controls, a projection comparison using seven sigma points versus 200 Monte Carlo samples, and an anchoring comparison using K=20 versus the existing default K=50. Previously stated main benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F substantially extends component validation through a rolling-shutter ablation, a noisy-LiDAR case study and direct projection checks against linearization and Monte Carlo sampling. Appendix E also adds an anchoring-neighborhood cost/quality analysis. These supplement the retained factorization, appearance, tiling, culling and beam-filtering analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added Monte Carlo sampling serves as a projection comparator, not an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries in Tables 1–7 are retained. Additions include AlignMiF's Table 1 row, Table 8 chamfer distances of 0.356/0.252/0.250 for linearization/Monte Carlo/SimULi, and Figure 11 PSNR of 32.32/33.73 without/with rolling shutter. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1's scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and Algorithms 1–3 retain their mathematical content. The added projection validation is empirical; no new formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about real-time camera/LiDAR simulation, automated tiling, factorization and rendering fidelity and speed. Added evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds an anchoring training-overhead limitation and possible mitigations, explains claimed memory benefits of factorization, and discusses applicability to non-spinning LiDAR. Appendix F further explains how factorization accommodates noisy LiDAR supervision without degrading camera quality.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents a global four-million-Gaussian cap, approximately 900 MB serialized model size and approximately 14 minutes of default anchoring overhead, reduced to six minutes with K=20. It also identifies the official AlignMiF implementation. These disclosures do not establish changes to the original training configuration.

R1.justification: v3 adds Tang et al.'s AlignMiF and acknowledges its separate modality features and treatment of misalignment. It qualifies the criticism of prior NeRF methods accordingly and distinguishes AlignMiF's feature-fusion inference cost from SimULi's factorized rendering.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact. Local additions cover AlignMiF, expanded appendix explanations and new Appendix F; the author order, contact block and conference header also change.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 11–13 and Table 8, expands Table 1 and reframes Figure 10. Figure 1 moves above the abstract, while Table 7 and existing appendix illustrations are grouped more closely with their explanations. Most main-text displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the paper through comparison with the relevant AlignMiF baseline, direct projection and rolling-shutter checks, and clearer disclosure of memory and anchoring costs. The main method and established results remain unchanged. Limited setup detail for the new projection experiment constrains the added evidence, but the improved validation and transparency support a modest overall gain.
